posts.author: Soul_Narrative_Games
Ms Littlefish
posts.body:
I’ve been blessed by the kindness of this forum. So, so much deeper than “internet friends.” Just…friends.
I received beautiful artwork from many of you.
I traded care packages with some of you.
I did collabs with a few of you.
I received genuine company when I was practically stuck in a hospital for the better part of two years.
My time here has been so much more complete and wholesome than anything else I’ve ever done online.

posts.author: Ms Littlefish
TeiRaven
posts.body:
The Christmas Jam makes my list of fondest memories here too, there was something really special about that. The Advent calendars as well--I couldn't use a lot of the resources, but it was amazing to see them. The skill and generosity of the artists here is absolutely off the charts.
Then there were the silly things, like the "words that don't exist" thread and that time Trihan told us how to talk about meeting a talking badger in the enchanted woods in Scottish. That might be the thing I'll miss most of all--the feeling of sitting my favorite coffee shop, listening to what's going on around me and piping up when I've got something to add. I'm going to miss this coffee shop.

posts.author: Piyan Glupak
posts.body:
This forum has really helped me extend what I can do with RPG Maker. I have had a huge amount of help. A lot was from looking at other people's threads, but some was from questions that I asked. This has also been my main source of information about plugins, either directly (plugin threads) or information in members' signatures about their own sites.
Can't call myself much of a programmer, but I doubt that I would have even dipped my toe into JavaScript without this forum.
The help that I have been able to offer in return has been limited. I have a little experience in using some plugins, and I was able to help with eventing sometimes. It has been nice getting people to a point where they have enough confidence to be able to cope largely on their own.

posts.author: SeaPhoenix
posts.body:
I loved the Advent Calendars. It was always a joy to see what each artist had in store for us every day, and I can only hope they enjoyed it too.
I learned a lot by participating in game jams here, and I don't know if I could have made my games without getting my start in them.
Finally, it was heartwarming to see people help each other out every day, by answering questions and offering feedback and support. It really felt like a community.
Thank you to everyone who shared their time, knowledge, and resources on this forum, including the mods!

posts.author: BobbyLily
posts.body:

Though I'll admit a good chunk of that enjoyment came from the fact that I won said jam.

posts.author: Darkmoon9
posts.body:
I will miss this place. You guys helped me with countless issues when I was a new developer. I know enough now about developing for rpg maker to get by. But help is probably not going to be as easy to find in the future. The new forums are alot harder to navigate. I hope organisation is improved over there or its gonna be hard to find anything.

posts.author: Madam_Detective
posts.body:
I really appreciate the people who gave me life advice when I didn't know who else to ask. There was a period when I flunked out of my dream major, and became depressed and suicidal. And then a few years later, I finally managed to graduate university with something worthwhile, I again asked for advice on what else I can do next with my life. Wouldn't say my life has been smooth sailing, but at least I am still living better than more than half the population of this planet.
They might be gone now, not sure if anyone them even came back to see the forum being closed, but I wish them good luck with their own life.

posts.author: Miss Nile
posts.body:
That one time I won a mapping contest, and the days when I used to post screenshots of my unfinished game on the Screenshots thread and received so much useful and constructive feedback. All the mapping requests I got and the wonderful people I worked with, the projects I helped. All these make such wonderful memories to me.
I am here since 2012. Maybe not the most active person ever but I used to lurk around and I love this place. I will miss it very, very much.

posts.author: Trihan
posts.body:
All the times I got a message from someone to thank me for my tutorial series, code snippets and plugins over the years, in some cases saying my help basically helped them stick with the hobby or saved a project they would have given up on.
The wonderful friendships and connections I've made in my time here, particularly
@ATT_Turan
. I have very fond memories of our interactions, both on posts and private conversations.
The opportunities being in this community has given me to playtest new games before release, contribute to commercial titles, and the current trajectory my career as a freelance coder is on (with a good chance of that becoming a full-time job later this year).
I wouldn't be the person I am without these forums and the people who use them. I'm not sure who I'll be when they're gone, but I'm confident we'll rebuild somewhere else.

I joined back in 2022 + this is the longest I've ever stayed on a website because of how. fun it is?
i would be completely lying if i said these weren't extremely rough years for me irl LMFAO but it was very reassuring that like, no matter what was going on, if i happened to peek in here i could see people celebrating that they finally got a map to look the right way, or complaining about some glitch i was trying to fix too... people improving their art, getting more confident in their game dev skills, seeing familiar faces + the usual suspects making funny replies in profile posts.

posts.author: Touchfuzzy
posts.body:
A long time ago, there was a user who insisted that all rules were awful and constraining, and that I was a "legal eagle" for insisting that he follow all the rules everyone else did. It's where the Lead Eagle joke came from.
Anyway, I told him that I wouldn't enforce any rules in one of his threads. Just that place. On the whole forum (I did have lines I would have moderated for, but I ignored all the basic rules). I have never seen a thread go to garbage so fast.
Probably not the best way to handle that situation, but it always makes me laugh to think back on it.
